podcast.title: Mentorship and Collaboration with Dolly Parton (1967-1974)
podcast.body: Porter Wagoner gave Dolly Parton her start in the music industry, and her career was linked with his from 1967. She performed on his TV show and was part of his touring company, recording approximately 12 albums with him. Wagoner reportedly relied heavily on Parton to sell records. "All right, Porter Wagner definitely had his own career and he definitely gave Dolly Parton her start in the industry. But Dolly and Porter together were a formidable recording team and I think he definitely relied on her to sell records."

podcast.title: Contract Dispute and $3 Million Lawsuit Against Dolly Parton (1979)
podcast.body: When Dolly Parton sought to leave their partnership in 1974, Wagoner initially refused to release her. He later sued her for $3 million in 1979, claiming breach of contract and demanding 15% of her net income and record royalties from 1974-1979. He accused her of being "selfish" and believed she owed him for her start in the industry. "Wagner sued Dolly for $3 million in 1979 saying that she broke their contract and he wanted 15% of her net income between June 1974 and June 1979 and he wanted 15% of her record royalties."

podcast.title: Career Launchpad for Dolly Parton
podcast.body: Porter Wagoner's television show is noted for being the platform that launched Dolly Parton's career. He was also a country star known for many country gospel songs, including "Pastor Absent on Vacation," which inspired Norman Greenbaum. "Wagner, whose TV show is notable for being the career launching pad for Dolly Parton."

podcast.title: Disapproval of Dolly Parton's Pop Crossover
podcast.body: Porter Wagoner publicly expressed his disapproval as Dolly Parton moved increasingly towards pop music in the late 1970s, reflecting a common sentiment among country purists at the time. "Dolly moved more toward pop as the 70s progressed which was again upsetting to many people in country music and Porter Wagner weighed in on it said he did not approve."

podcast.title: Dolly Parton's Early Career Mentor
podcast.body: Dolly Parton made her first appearances on Porter Wagoner's TV show. Wagoner expressed hope that Dolly would not move too far toward pop music, a wish she ultimately did not adhere to. "Despite Porter Wagner saying he really hoped that Dolly would not go too far toward pop, that is exactly what she was trying to do."

podcast.title: KRAK Radio Station Staple
podcast.body: Porter Wagoner was listed as a staple artist on KRAK, a country and western radio station managed by Allan Torbert, and represented the type of performer appreciated by country music purists. "Eddie Arnold, Buck Owens, Porter Wagner. I mean, these were KRAK staples."
